one_line: Early 15th‑century Tripura hill ruler, remembered as the founder of the historical Manikya line.

appearance.age_look: Mid-30s, athletic and wiry, used to marching in rugged hill terrain.
appearance.face: Oval face with high cheekbones and a straight nose, medium-brown complexion with a faint sun-browned tan, sharp dark eyes under slightly arched brows, a neat trimmed moustache with a short goatee, and a calm but alert default expression that tightens into focus in battle.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair gathered into a high knotted topknot at the back of the crown, wrapped with a narrow red cloth band; the front and sides are smooth and tidy with a few loose strands near the temples, and no helmet unless going into battle.
appearance.costume: He wears a knee-length off‑white cotton angarkha-style tunic that overlaps and ties to the right with simple cloth ties, its edges piped with narrow red borders; over this is a sleeveless rust‑red quilted cotton vest that serves as light armour, stitched in vertical channels; his lower garment is a dark green woven cotton dhoti wrapped above the ankles in a practical hill style with neat front pleats, secured at the waist with a broad brown leather belt bearing a simple bronze buckle and a small pouch; across his torso he wears a diagonal dark‑brown leather strap from left shoulder to right hip to support his weapon scabbard; his feet are in sturdy brown leather sandals with thong straps and side lacing suited for hill paths; on his wrists are a pair of plain bronze bangles and on his upper right arm a single slim armband; around his neck hangs a modest string of small polished carnelian and shell beads, with a single round copper pendant hinting at the early “Manikya” regnal style without becoming ostentatious regalia.
appearance.signature: A slightly curved, single-edged steel sword in a plain dark-brown leather scabbard, about forearm to hand in length like a light tulwar precursor, with a simple bronze crossguard and a wooden hilt wrapped in dark cord, worn slung at his left hip on the diagonal strap and often resting in his right hand as he gives orders.

ref_desc: Chhengthung Fa is a mid‑30s medium‑brown man with an oval face, neat moustache and goatee, black hair in a high topknot with a red band, wearing an off‑white tunic, rust‑red quilted vest, dark green dhoti, brown leather belt and strap, bronze ornaments, and carrying a curved steel sword in a brown leather scabbard at his left hip.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full‑body anime‑style character sheet of Chhengthung Fa, an early 15th‑century Tripura hill ruler in realistic historical dress: a mid‑30s medium‑brown man with an oval face, high cheekbones, sharp dark eyes, and a neat trimmed moustache with a short goatee, his thick black hair pulled into a high knotted topknot wrapped with a narrow red cloth band and a few loose strands at the temples. Show him in an off‑white knee‑length cotton angarkha tunic tying to the right with red piping on the edges, over which he wears a rust‑red sleeveless quilted cotton vest stitched in vertical channels like light armour. His lower body is covered by a dark green woven cotton dhoti wrapped neatly to just above the ankles, secured by a broad brown leather belt with a simple bronze buckle and a small pouch, with a dark‑brown leather strap crossing diagonally from left shoulder to right hip to support his weapon. Give him sturdy brown leather sandals suited for hills, plain bronze bangles on both wrists, a slim bronze armband on his upper right arm, and a modest necklace of small carnelian and shell beads with a single round copper pendant. His signature weapon is a slightly curved single‑edged steel sword with a plain bronze crossguard and a wooden hilt wrapped in dark cord, sheathed in a dark‑brown leather scabbard hanging at his left hip from the diagonal strap; include one pose with the sword sheathed and another with it lightly held in his right hand as he stands in a calm yet commanding stance. Emphasise the off‑white, rust red, dark green, brown leather and bronze colour palette, keeping the overall look dignified, modest and historically grounded without fantasy elements.
